Bhante, in 'The Most Precious GIft' (Standing Meditation), what is the core doctrinal teaching regarding 'This guided meditation was offered on'?

In this section from *The Most Precious GIft*, the master explains: *"This guided meditation was offered on 22 November 2014."*. From the perspective of the Four Noble Truths, suffering arises whenever the mind grasps at impermanent phenomena (*anicca*) as a reliable self (*atta*). By establishing clear comprehension (*sampajañña*) and seeing conditioned events as empty of inherent ownership, craving (*taṇhā*) is unhooked. It is like grasping a poisonous cobra by the tail: tempting and sleek from afar, but deadly the moment you grasp it. Release the tail and live in safety. Anchor your understanding in direct seeing rather than speculative theory.

In sitting meditation, how do we work with the body and breath when 'The Most Precious GIft' advises: 'You may not get every detail'?

The practical guidance given in *The Most Precious GIft* instructs: *"You may not get every detail but you can sense the feet on the floor; feel the nice sensation there."*. When you sit on the cushion, do not wage war against wandering thoughts. First ground attention in the physical posture—soften the belly, relax the face, and allow the breath to find its natural rhythm. When thoughts arise, notice the space around them rather than following the story. It is like still, flowing water (nam lai rin): awareness flows smoothly perceiving sights and sounds, while the heart inside remains utterly motionless. Rest the mind gently in the rhythm of each natural in-and-out breath.

How does 'The Most Precious GIft' (Standing Meditation) point to Not-Self (Anattā) and unconditioned peace in the statement: 'Just as you swept downwards, you'?

The profound pointer offered in *The Most Precious GIft* reveals: *"Just as you swept downwards, you can then extend your awareness by climbing up from the soles of the feet, as if there’s a line of awareness drawing up through the legs, gathering in the lower abdomen and rising up the trunk of the body into the throat and the back of the head."*. Look directly at the awareness that knows this present moment: the knowing itself has no gender, no nationality, no age, and no suffering. All physical sensations, thoughts, and emotions are merely visitors moving through this open sky of awareness. When you stop claiming ownership over what arises and ceases, liberation is right here. It is like birds flying through the open sky: they leave no footprints, and the vast space remains uncolored and untethered by their passing. Rest as the peaceful, unmoving knowing.
